title: Granular attribution reconciler for per-route/model/customer cost & latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers and internal teams need an accurate, auditable breakdown of inference cost and latency per API route, model variant, and customer. Existing rollups conflate multi-step requests, cache hits, and background reconciliation delays which causes imbalance between billed usage and console-visible cost allocation.

Goal: Build a reconciliation service ("Granular Attribution Reconciler") that ingests telemetry and billing events, attributes cost and latency deterministically to (route, model_variant, customer_id), surfaces per-route/model/customer breakdowns in materialized views, and emits reconciled deltas for the billing system and console UI.

Requirements and constraints:
- Attribution must account for: token generation cost, KV/prefix cache reuse, multi-model cascades (e.g., reranking + generation), and amortized GPU init and batch overhead.
- Latency decomposition to include: client-to-edge, queue_wait, model_inference, kernel_setup, and downstream aggregation time (for multi-call routes).
- Support both streaming (near-real-time dashboards) and batch reconciliation (strong consistency for billing).
- Provide deterministic idempotent attribution so replays and late-arriving telemetry converge to the same allocation.
- Keep reconciliation window configurable (default 24 hours) to allow for delayed traces and billing events.
- Keep customer-visible numbers explainable: tie each billed token/unit to the attribution path and store a small audit sample for 30 days.

High-level design:
1) Ingest: telemetry and cost signals come from two sources: Kafka topic (telemetry: traces, per-request timing, model variant used, cache hit tags) and billing events from the usage aggregator (daily rollups with raw token counts and GPU-hour amortization).
2) Stream pre-aggregation: Flink job performs per-request enrichment (join by request_id), computes preliminary attribution vectors (per-call token counts, cache_hit_flags, model_variant_id), and writes compact proto records to a reconciler topic.
3) Reconciler service: batch consumer that materializes per-request attribution into BigQuery (or ClickHouse) staging tables and runs a two-pass allocation: fast-path allocation for >95% of requests (single-model non-streaming) and slow-path for cascades and cross-route fanouts.
4) Reconciliation and delta emission: run deterministic aggregation over the reconciliation window, compute deltas against last-published allocations, and emit correction events for billing and console analytics.
5) Materialized views: create per-customer, per-route, per-model materialized views for console queries and export to the dashboard pipeline. Views include: total_cost, token_count, median_latency, p95_latency, pct_cache_hits, and attribution_breakdown (list of contributing models).
6) Audit & sampling: persist a sampled set of raw attribution traces (redacted PII) to a secure store for debugging and compliance (30d retention).

Key algorithmic details (unique aspects):
- Cache-aware cost splitting: when a prefix/KV cache is used, only incremental tokens are charged to the caller; cost of cached responses is amortized to the originator that primed the cache according to a configurable decay window.
- Batch overhead amortization: for batched inference we split GPU time between requests proportional to their token contribution and estimated compute weight; kernel startup fixed-costs are distributed by request arrival ordering to preserve determinism.
- Multi-call causality graphs: represent each API call as a small DAG of model calls; attribution walks the DAG and attributes upstream costs to the originating route, with special handling for shared rerankers (split proportionally by candidate scores).
- Latency tail attribution: to explain p95/p99 we track span-level signals and annotate the materialized rows with the dominant contributor span and its share of the wall-clock time.

Storage & query pattern decisions:
- Staging: compact proto rows in BigQuery partitioned by ingestion_date and request_hour for efficient backfills.
- MVs: daily materialized views in ClickHouse for low-latency console queries (cold storage in BigQuery for long-term audits).
- Cost of cross-join avoidance: precompute per-request coarse keys (route+model+customer) so dashboard queries never do large joins at runtime.

Acceptance criteria:
- Reconciler produces per-route/model/customer breakdowns with <=0.5% divergence vs oracle billing model for a 48h test window.
- Console shows near-real-time (<=30s) updates for common routes and eventual consistency for reconciliation deltas within 24h.
- Unit and integration tests for deterministic allocation logic and replay idempotency.
- Security review completed for audit store and redaction pipeline.

Out of scope for initial rollout: UI work to display full causal DAG, per-token lineage export, and per-request audit downloads (these are follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Per-route/model/customer totals match billing rollups within 0.5% over 48h test
Streaming dashboard latency <= 30s for 90% of common routes
Reconciliation deltas reconcile within 24h by default
Deterministic replay produces identical allocations for repeated runs
Security review signed off for audit sampling store
updates: 2025-02-20: Design review with PM/Infra. Decided on Flink for enrichment and a batch reconciler for strong consistency. Action: Michael to prototype Flink join with request_id (Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/GRANULAR-ATTRIB).

2025-02-26: Prototype completed for streaming enrichment; wrote test harness that joins telemetry+billing by request_id. Results: 12ms median per-record enrichment. Follow-up: add cache-aware attribution logic. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/reconciler/pull/187)

2025-03-04: Spike for batch allocation algorithms compared 3 amortization strategies. Chose proportional token-weight split because it is explainable and stable for small batches. Notes saved: https://gist.github.com/mchen/attrib-spike
2025-03-09: Security kickoff for audit sampling. Identified PII fields to redact and signed NDA for vendor storage. SRE asked for rate-limited writes to ClickHouse. (Ticket: SEC-401)

2025-03-12: Integration test wired: streaming enrichment -> reconciler staging -> MV materialization. Found an edge-case with late-arriving billing events; added 48h grace window and tombstone markers. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/reconciler/pull/202)
notes: Related work: ties into ENG-11807 billing rollup; ensure schema compatibility with the rollup producer.
We will expose a debugging endpoint that returns sample attribution traces for support engineers (RBAC-protected).
Monitoring: add metrics for reconciliation lag, allocation-delta-rate, and idempotency conflicts. Create Grafana dashboards under console-analytics team.
Open question: how to present amortized GPU startup cost in per-request UI without confusing customers. PM prefers an opt-in breakdown toggle.
